# Appendix: the architectural constants

[← dictionary index](index.md)

The numbers of the processor status word, the modes, the exception vectors, the page-table entry, the memory types, the translation geometry, the system registers, and the addressing modes, each read from the machine-readable specification (`spec/grammars.d/50-system-v1.hbnf` and `spec/grammars.d`).

*Generated by `tools/mkmanual.py`; do not edit.*

## The processor status word (16 bits)

| Field | Bit | Width | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `T` | 4 | 1 | trace: take a trace trap after the next instruction |
| `PRI` | 5 | 3 | interrupt priority level, 0 to 7 |
| `MODE` | 8 | 2 | current mode |
| `PREV` | 10 | 2 | previous mode (the mode before the last exception) |

Bits 0 to 3 and 12 to 15 are reserved and read as zero: the machine has no condition codes.

## The modes

| Mode | Value |
|---|---|
| kernel | 0 |
| supervisor | 1 |
| user | 3 |

Value 2 is reserved: loading it into either mode field of the status word is an illegal instruction.

## The exception vectors

The table has 512 entries of eight bytes at the physical address `VBR + 8 * vector`; `ECAUSE` equals the vector number.

| Vector | Number | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `RESET` | 0 | processor reset: the first instruction fetch |
| `MACHINE_CHECK` | 1 | an unrecoverable error (a posted write that timed out, an uncorrectable memory error, a failed vector fetch); not restartable |
| `ILLEGAL` | 2 | a reserved or undefined opcode, a reserved encoding or an unassigned system register |
| `PRIVILEGED` | 3 | a system instruction executed outside kernel mode |
| `MISALIGNED` | 4 | an atomic, `PUSHX`, `POPX` or the operand of a vector block at an address that is not a multiple of its size, or `MCOL`, `MCOLRD` or `MCOLWR` with an address or a count that is not a multiple of its granule block (a plain load or store has no alignment fault) |
| `NONCANONICAL` | 5 | a virtual address whose bits 59 to 39 differ from bit 38 (bits 63 to 60 are the colour of the pointer) |
| `IFAULT` | 6 | instruction fetch from a page that is not mapped |
| `LFAULT` | 7 | load from a page that is not mapped |
| `SFAULT` | 8 | store to a page that is not mapped |
| `IPROT` | 9 | instruction fetch denied by the page permissions |
| `LPROT` | 10 | load denied by the page permissions, or by the colour check: the pointer's colour differs from the granule's (6.8.7) |
| `SPROT` | 11 | store denied by the page permissions, or by the colour check (6.8.7) |
| `DIVZERO` | 12 | division by zero (`DIV`, `DIVU`, `MOD`, `MODU`) |
| `BUSFAULT` | 13 | a read of non-existent memory (a precise abort) |
| `LPAD` | 14 | an indirect transfer that did not land on `LPAD` (enforcement off in ABI version 1) |
| `BPT` | 15 | the `BPT` instruction |
| `CHECK` | 16 | a failed run-time check (the compare-and-trap, `CHK2`, `ADDV`, `SUBV`, `MULV`) |
| `HEXIT` | 17 | the instruction exit of a guest, in the hypervisor's vector table only (6.17.16) |
| `GIFAULT` | 18 | a guest-physical instruction fault (stage 2), in the hypervisor's table only |
| `GLFAULT` | 19 | a guest-physical load fault (stage 2), in the hypervisor's table only |
| `GSFAULT` | 20 | a guest-physical store fault (stage 2), in the hypervisor's table only |
| `IRQ_BASE` | 32 | the first interrupt vector |
| `TIMER` | 32 | the timer interrupt (level 6) |
| `CONSOLE_IN` | 33 | console receive interrupt (level 4) |
| `CONSOLE_OUT` | 34 | console transmit interrupt (level 4) |
| `PCIE_INTA` | 35 | PCI Express interrupt pin A of the model host bridge (level 5) |
| `PCIE_INTB` | 36 | PCI Express interrupt pin B (level 5) |
| `PCIE_INTC` | 37 | PCI Express interrupt pin C (level 5) |
| `PCIE_INTD` | 38 | PCI Express interrupt pin D (level 5) |
| `IOMMU` | 39 | the IOMMU unit's own interrupt, a wired line (level 5; 2.11.11) |
| `TRAP_BASE` | 256 | `TRAP $n` enters vector 256 + n |
| `COUNT` | 512 | the number of vectors; the table has this many eight-byte entries |

## The page-table entry (64 bits)

| Field | Bit | Width | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `V` | 0 | 1 | valid |
| `R` | 1 | 1 | readable |
| `W` | 2 | 1 | writable |
| `X` | 3 | 1 | executable |
| `U` | 4 | 1 | accessible from user mode |
| `G` | 5 | 1 | global: ignores the ASID |
| `A` | 6 | 1 | accessed (managed by software) |
| `D` | 7 | 1 | dirty (managed by software) |
| `MT` | 8 | 2 | memory type |
| `PPN` | 12 | 28 | physical page number: physical address bits 12 to 39, in place |

A non-leaf entry has `V` = 1 and `R` = `W` = `X` = 0 and points to the next table. Every bit not named is zero.

## The memory types (`MT`)

| Type | Value |
|---|---|
| cached | 0 |
| uncached | 1 |
| device weak | 2 |
| device | 3 |

| va bits | 39 |
| pa bits | 40 |
